There are 25,780,971 businesses on Google Maps in the US right now. Only 8,851,466 of them have a public email address you can actually reach. Guess which ones your competitors are writing to?

Here's the part nobody says out loud, though. When you search how to create an email list in Gmail, the list is the easy bit. Gmail — yes, the tab you already have open in another window — can build one right inside your Gmail inbox in about four minutes. Filling that list with people worth emailing? That's where the real work hides.

So this is a guide to both halves. Three ways to create a mailing list in Gmail, the sending limits that will ruin your afternoon if you don't know them, a quick honest word on what a **gmail mailing list** can't do, and then the thing every other tutorial skips: where the contacts come from. Four minutes for the container. Let's talk about the contents too.

## What Is an Email List in Gmail (and What It Isn't)

Gmail doesn't have a feature called "email list." It never has. What it has is something better named — and more limited — than you'd think.

When people ask **how do I make a mailing list in Gmail**, they usually mean one of three things, and mixing them up is where the confusion starts. A **contact label** is an addressing shortcut: it drops a bunch of addresses into your To or Bcc field in one go. A **Google Group** is a genuine shared address with its own inbox and archive. A **dedicated tool** is a full sending platform with tracking and unsubscribe management. Same goal, wildly different machines.

Most of the time, "email list," "distribution list," and "contact group" all point at the first one — the humble contact label. That's the answer to **how to create a group email in Gmail** for 90% of people. But knowing the difference between a contact label and a Google Group saves you from picking the wrong tool for the job. So here's the plain version.

|     | Contact label | Google Group | Dedicated tool |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Setup time | ~4 minutes | ~15 minutes | An afternoon |
| Replies go to | Only you | The whole group | You (with tracking) |
| Shared archive | No  | Yes | Varies |
| Unsubscribe handling | Manual | Self-service | Automatic |
| Best for | Quick sends | Two-way conversation | Real outreach at scale |

Got it? Good. Now the four-minute version.

## Method 1 — Create an Email List With Google Contacts Labels (4 Minutes)

This is the method 90% of people are looking for. It takes four minutes and it's free. This is also the answer to **how to make a group email in Gmail** and, honestly, to **create a mailing list in Gmail** — same feature, different search box.

You don't do any of this inside Gmail, by the way. You do it in [Google Contacts](https://contacts.google.com/), which is a separate app most people forget exists. Open it in a new tab and follow along.

### Step 1 — Open Google Contacts

Head to `contacts.google.com` and sign in with the same account you send email from. If your contacts look thin, don't panic — you can add people as you go, or import a whole file (more on that in Method 3).

### Step 2 — Select your contacts

Hover over a contact's photo and a checkbox appears. Tick everyone you want on the list. On a laptop this is the fastest way to **make a group in Gmail on computer** — click, click, click, done.

### Step 3 — Create the label

With your contacts selected, click the label icon at the top, then "Create label." Name it something you'll recognize in six months — "Dallas Plumbers Q3," not "list2final." This label _is_ your list. That's it. You just built a **gmail distribution list**.

### Step 4 — Send to your list from Gmail

Back in Gmail, hit Compose and start typing the label name in the To field. Gmail auto-suggests it and expands every contact behind it in one click. This is **how to email a label in Gmail**, and it works the same whether you've got 8 people or 800. On mobile it's nearly identical — **how to send email to a label group in the Gmail app** is the same move: compose, type the label name, tap it.

**Bcc vs To — read this before you send.** Put the label in the **To** field and every recipient sees every other address. Fine for your project team. A privacy disaster for prospects. Put it in **Bcc** instead — with your own address in To — and everyone's hidden from everyone else. This is exactly **how to create a group email in Gmail without recipients showing**, and it's the same trick as sending a **group email in Gmail using Bcc**. The catch? Replies come back only to you. Group conversation is off the table.

### How to add or remove contacts from your list later

Lists change. To handle **how to add contacts to a group in Gmail** after the fact: open Google Contacts, select the new people, click the label icon, tick your label. Done. To remove someone, open their card, click the label, untick it. That's also the answer to **how to remove someone from a Gmail mailing list** — there's no fancy unsubscribe button, you just untick the box yourself.

# How to Get Contacts for a Cold Email Campaign?

Want to start B2B email list building for your outreach campaign, but don't know how and where to source the information from? Read our complete guide to get started.

Cleverviral

·

September 25, 2023

·

8 min

When I first dipped my toes in the dynamic world of B2B prospecting, there was one particular question that kept me up all the time: How to get contacts for a cold email campaign? Being a relative beginner, it was quite a task and it took me a long while to figure out the best way to find email addresses for lead generation.

As is clear, B2B email list building is what drives your outreach efforts, and it's important to be proactive about it if you want to grow your business with cold outreach. 

Whether you're just starting or trying to refine your approach, the subsequent sections will explore how you can get your prospects’ data in an effortless manner. We’ll also cover a few B2B list building tools to bolster your prospecting. 

Let’s get started.  

## What is a prospect email list?

At its core, a prospect email list is nothing but a list of potential individuals and decision-makers you want to work with. These are people who could benefit from using your product or service and usually have the buying power to avail it. 

In the context of B2B prospecting, this list includes details such as the company name, position or title of contact alongside their industry and location. Based on the level of details required, you can also source it through various other sources. 

This process of creating and maintaining a prospect list is called B2B email list building – and is an essential component of B2B outbound sales.   

## How to find someone's email address for free?

In the high-stakes world of B2B prospecting, finding a prospect's email address can often feel like looking for a needle in a haystack. But what if you could find that needle without spending a dime? 

There are multiple free methods to start collecting prospect emails for the purpose of B2B email list building. Some of them we’ve used and found success with are as follows: 

### LinkedIn

![How to find prospect info on LinkedIn for B2B email list building ](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6a57555d2a7c5259b5a4223c/6a5bf4faa9941b70043809d2_6a594b32b454a68b947ea640_Email-List-Building-LinkedIn.png)

Apart from helping you connect with professionals, LinkedIn is also a crucial tool for B2B email list building. Having done LinkedIn outreach for multiple clients at our company, you can simply leverage LinkedIn search to find your prospect’s email address for free.

All you need to do is search their name on LinkedIn. Usually people also add their email address to their LinkedIn account. You can then send them a connection request, and once accepted, copy & paste their email from the ‘Contact Info’ section.  

### Company Website

Another popular free method for B2B email list building is by using the company website. Many companies provide email addresses of key decision-makers on their website itself. I know this sounds simple, but it's one of the most effective B2B prospecting methods. 

You can find this information on the ‘About Us’ or ‘Team’ section of the prospect’s website.   

### Google Search

A simple Google search is more powerful than you think. Especially when it comes to B2B email list building. If you’re looking for B2B prospecting data, simply run an advanced Google search in the following combinations:

*   **_\[name\] + contact (or) contact information (or) contact me_**
*   **_\[name\] + email (or) email address_**

That being said, you can also run a website-wide search by using the following search combinations:

*   **_site: companywebsite.com + \[name\] + email_**
*   **_site: companywebsite.com + \[name\] + contact_**

Here are some other ways to find B2B prospecting data with a Google search:

a. **Adding Personal Information:** You can also add the prospect’s personal information to your search for more refined results. This is a useful tactic, especially when you’re searching for prospects with similar names or spellings (as is the case with names in the UK, US & Europe markets).

When using this method, you can add personal information such as their hometown, profession, company name etc.

To do this, simply search using the following combination: **_\[name\] + email + hometown, or \[name\] + email + profession._**

b. **Adding LinkedIn or ZoomInfo:** LinkedIn and ZoomInfo are two of the most popular and widely-used B2B prospecting platforms.

You can simply run a Google search by adding “LinkedIn” or “ZoomInfo” to the prospect’s name in the following manner:

**_\[name\] + LinkedIn or \[name\] + ZoomInfo_**  

### WhoIs Search

WhoIs.com is a popular domain search engine which can also be used for the purpose of B2B email list building. This method of B2B prospecting involves entering the domain name of your prospect’s website to find more information about them.

Once through, you can find the prospect’s email under the **‘Registrant Contact’** section.

While useful, this cold list building method isn’t failure-proof. When registering for a domain, people sometimes don’t share their emails publicly.

If this is the case with your prospect, it can lead to a waste of valuable time and resources.

### Using a Browser Extension

Another extremely useful way to find contact details of your prospects is to use browser extensions from the likes of [Hunter.io](https://hunter.io/), [RocketReach](https://rocketreach.co/) and [RevDriver (by Salesintel)](https://salesintel.io/integrations/chrome-integration/) These tools help you with efficient B2B email list building, scraping contact information from their LinkedIn profiles and even web pages.  
  
Apart from the prospect's email address, some of these tools also help you source their phone numbers and other firmographic and technographic data.

In the previous section, we discussed how to build a prospect list with free resources. Another highly-efficient method to get started with B2B email list building is to start using email finder tools. While the free resources are useful, they often end up taking a lot of time.

If you’re a B2B marketer looking to save time, a B2B list building tool is the way to go.
